Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment Dry, sharp-lapse-rate day with no precipitation and no föhn. Thermals are strongest at McClellan, Hallelujah, Rainbow Ridge, and West McClellan, but usable windows depend on wind-direction timing. Freezing level is high at 15,725 ft MSL, and overdevelopment is 0% at all named sites.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — brief SE-aligned window 11am–noon before winds turn N/NW; peak w* 307 ft/min, thermal ceiling 2270 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — best late when W/NW flow aligns; 4pm–5pm; peak w* 413 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6658 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable — light S flow and early thermals; 10am–2pm; peak w* 330 ft/min, thermal ceiling 2225 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • McClellan: Favorable — strongest thermals and highest ceiling; 1pm–5pm; peak w* 467 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6854 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • West McClellan: Marginal — thermals peak before preferred W flow, leaving only a late short window; 3pm–5pm; peak w* 429 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5832 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • Peavine Mountain: Favorable — consistent S flow and moderate thermals; 10am–4pm; peak w* 373 ft/min, thermal ceiling 3615 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — E flow on launch with good thermals; 12pm–5pm; peak w* 437 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6234 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • Duck Hill: Favorable — late W/NW flow and good thermals; 3pm–5pm; peak w* 392 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5542 ft AGL; sharp-thermal caution (advanced only).
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable — no thermal development; peak w* 0 ft/min, only a brief 5pm SW 2 mph ridge puff, PBLH 84 ft AGL.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals: regional lapse rate 9.9 °C/km; site lapse rates 9.3–10.0 °C/km at thermal sites — advanced/expert only.
  • Icing: possible only on high climbs; freezing level 15,725 ft MSL, with domain-wide thermal ceiling up to 17,417 ft MSL.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
